instruction: Switch to natural scrolling (also called reverse scrolling) for the touchpad on my Ubuntu system.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires enabling natural scrolling for touchpad. Setup disables natural-scroll (false), agent must enable it (true). Uses existing vm_command_line getter and exact_match metric. Verified: gsettings returns 'true\n' when enabled.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly extracts the natural-scroll setting using vm_command_line getter with the appropriate gsettings command
Expected value 'true\n' is semantically correct - task requires enabling natural scrolling, and setup disables it (false), so agent must change it to true
exact_match metric is appropriate for comparing gsettings output which is deterministic
Complete coverage: instruction has single requirement (enable natural scrolling) and evaluator verifies exactly that state
No state timing issues: gsettings values persist and don't require UI interaction or postconfig
Data flow is correct: getter extracts right state → metric compares correctly → expected value matches task requirement
